findings.plain: If someone forgot to switch off try-out mode online, anyone on the internet could open the test mailbox, read the owner's sign-in code and take over the board. Now the test mailbox only opens for someone at the same computer, and closes as soon as a real email service is set up.
In try-out mode, a broken request showed an error page with the program's insides (file paths on this computer). Errors are now a short plain message.
The board pages had no extra browser lock against harmful code. They now tell the browser to run only the board's own code, so even a slipped-through trick in a post could not run.

There is no limit on how many posts, replies or votes one signed-in person can make per hour. A spammer could flood the board until you block them in the Owner's room. Worth adding later with Change something.
Sign-ins never expire. Sign out ends it on that device, and blocking a person stops their posting, but there is no automatic time-out yet.
Pasted pictures stay on the server even when a post is deleted, and many accounts together could slowly fill the disk. Keep an eye on the data folder size.

ok: No passwords, keys or tokens in the code or anywhere in its history (the checks use an obviously fake key, sk-ant-test).
.env is listed in .gitignore, so settings with secrets are never committed. The data folder (database and pictures) is ignored too.
There are no passwords at all. Sign-in codes and sign-ins are stored only as scrambled fingerprints, codes last 10 minutes and stop after 5 wrong tries.
The Owner's room and all owner actions need the owner's sign-in. Email addresses are only shown to the owner.
Everything people type goes into the database safely (no raw text in queries) and is shown as safe text: HTML and javascript: links are made harmless.
Pictures are checked by what they really are (no SVG), and only Lemonaid's own pictures can show in posts.
The package check (npm audit) finds 0 known security problems.

where.name: Render (runs it for you, about $7.25 a month)
where.why: Lemonaid has a server and keeps data, so it needs a host that runs Node.js and keeps a disk. Render does that and everything is set up on its website, nothing to type in a terminal. Its free plan has no lasting disk, so it needs the Starter plan plus a 1 GB disk.
steps: First put the code in a GitHub repository (see 'Share the code' below), or keep it private there if you prefer.
Make an account at render.com and connect it to your GitHub account.
Press New, then Web Service, and pick the Lemonaid repository.
Set Build command to: npm install. Set Start command to: npm start. Pick the Starter plan.
Under Disks, add a disk with mount path /var/data and size 1 GB.
Make an account at brevo.com (free), add and verify your email domain, and open SMTP & API to get your SMTP login and key.

In Render, under Environment, add: NODE_ENV = production, OWNER_EMAIL = your email, PUBLIC_URL = your Render address (like https://lemonaid-xxxx.onrender.com), SMTP_URL = smtp://YOUR-LOGIN:YOUR-KEY@smtp-relay.brevo.com:587, MAIL_FROM = Lemonaid <hello@yourdomain.com>, DATA_DIR = /var/data, TRUST_PROXY = 1.
Optional: add ANTHROPIC_API_KEY (from console.anthropic.com) for the AI check.
Press Deploy. When it is live, open the address, sign in with your owner email, and copy the one line from the demo page into your website.
Optional: under Settings, add your own address like board.yourdomain.com and update PUBLIC_URL to match.

where.name: A small server of your own (about $5 a month, or one you already have)
where.why: Cheapest and fully yours, and it can sit next to your other sites. It needs typing commands in a terminal to set up, so pick this if you or a helper are comfortable with that.
steps: Rent a small Linux server (for example at hetzner.com or digitalocean.com), or use the one you already run your sites on.
Install Node.js 22.13 or newer and git on it.
Copy the project there, run npm install, and copy .env.example to .env and fill it in (the README explains each line).
Keep it running with a service manager (for example pm2 or systemd) using npm start.
Put it behind your web server (Caddy, nginx or Traefik) with HTTPS on an address like board.yourdomain.com, and set TRUST_PROXY=1.
Back up the data folder regularly.

where.name: Share the code as open source (GitHub, free)
where.why: This is how others get Lemonaid to run their own copy. Everything is done on the website, and the README already explains setup and the licence is MIT.
steps: Make an account at github.com if you do not have one.
Press New repository, name it lemonaid, choose Public, and do not add a README or licence (the project has them).
Use GitHub Desktop (desktop.github.com) to add this project folder and Publish it to that repository.
Check on GitHub that only the project files are there: no .env file, no data folder, no .claude folder and no 'Open lemonaid.bat'. (They are not committed now; keep it that way.)
Add a short description and topics like feedback, forum, issues, embed.

said: Fixed 1 must and 2 smaller safety problems. 3 things to know (no posting limits yet, sign-ins never expire, pictures can pile up). Ready to put online.
